key_insight: Thermally sprayed oxide coatings on 304 stainless steel can act as effective barriers against molten Al-based phase change materials, maintaining compatibility and stability under static exposure and thermal cycling.
engineering_relevance: This work supports the design of durable container linings for high-temperature latent heat thermal energy storage using aluminium-based mPCMs.
method: APS Al2O3, ZrO2, and Al2O3/ZrO2 coatings were deposited directly onto 304 stainless steel.
HVSFS was used to produce an Al2O3 coating with more uniform thickness distribution than APS.
Coatings were tested by long-term static molten-alloy exposure, thermal cycling, and liquid thermal contact resistance measurements.
evidence_signal: After two weeks of static exposure there was no reaction layer, coating dissolution, or detectable interdiffusion; the Al2O3/Al-12.3 wt.% Si system also showed no degradation after about 300 thermal cycles.
watch_item: The results are promising but are based on specific coating compositions, substrate, and test conditions, so scale-up and long-term service behavior still need validation.
paper_title: Thermal Sprayed Oxide Coatings for Stainless Steel Containers Used with Molten Al–Si and Al–Cu–Si Phase Change Materials: Compatibility and Thermal Cycling Stability
